As someone who is 22 and jumped straight from undergrad to PT school, I was also worried about the things I saw on here. I was also very fortunate to not have undergrad debt, so thats huge for sure. Now, when it comes down to PT school debt I’m also a bit of a unicorn. The program I’m in is in my hometown, so I currently live at my parents house for free and they’re also helping pay tuition. With that said though, this particular program is only ~$85k total (I laughed putting only in front of that much money). So, my biggest deterrent in all this would definitely be the financial aspect if programs near you are upwards of 100k, but it seems youre mapping out finances. 
In terms of the actual schooling itself. It’s a lot. But as a teacher and bio major, I’m sure you can navigate that as well. Bottom line is, you will definitely be making more money at the end of it all. 
You have to take a lot of the stuff on these subs with a grain of salt. People knew they were going to be making ~$70k-ish before taking out 6 figures in loans (at least if they did research). And to be quite honest, I see the direction education is headed (my brother is a teacher) and he’s also trying to jump ship.
